items.title: The verb tells with from and
items.caption: Every word except the verb stays the same. The singular verb leaves one doer with a companion, while the plural verb makes both people doers.

states.label: With
states.sm: Sā nofo le tama ma le teine.
states.en: The boy stayed with the girl.

states.label: And
states.sm: Sā nonofo le tama ma le teine.
states.en: The boy and the girl stayed.

items.title: One word, two jobs
items.caption: A singular verb keeps the companion outside the doer count. A plural verb shows that both joined names do the action.

cells.sm: Sā alu le teine ma le uō.
cells.en: The girl went with the friend.

cells.sm: Sā fāgota le tama ma le vaʻa.
cells.en: The boy went fishing with the canoe.

cells.sm: Sā nonofo le tama ma le teine.
cells.en: The boy and the girl stayed.

items.title: Choose one doer or two
items.intro: Read the English and choose the complete printed sentence that gives *ma* the intended job.

prompts.en: The boy stayed with the girl.

options.sm: Sā nofo le tama ma le teine.
Sā nonofo le tama ma le teine.

prompts.why: The singular verb leaves the girl as the companion.

prompts.en: The boy and the girl stayed.

options.sm: Sā nofo le tama ma le teine.
Sā nonofo le tama ma le teine.

prompts.why: The plural verb shows that both joined people are doers.
